newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Finland's Niinisto sees obligation to join EMU.
newsitem.headline: Finland's Niinisto sees obligation to join EMU.

text.p: Finnish Finance Minister Sauli Niinisto said his country had an obligation to join economic and monetary union (EMU) as it fulfilled all the necessary Maastricht treaty criteria to qualify for the single currency.

Niinisto, participating in a meeting of Centrist leaders in Brussels, noted that Finland before it joined the EU in 1995 had issued a reservation saying Finnish participatiion depended on parliament approval.
"Now that we meet all the criteria we are also discussing what the reservation means because we have an obligation (to join)," Niinisto told Reuters.

Only Britain and Denmark have the formal possibility to opt out from EMU, a key element of the Maastricht treaty, although Sweden insists its national parliament will decide this autumn on whether the country joins in 1999.
Niinisto also said the debate in parliament on the issue had not been as critical as he had expected. "It has been a good discussion," he said.
